notes: Killed while practising a hillclimb in the Freikaiserwagen, less than two months after he had driven a Maserati in the 1950 British Grand Prix. The article gives 29 July 1950 as the date of death and does not describe a mechanical failure.

He had already finished a world-championship race at Monaco in 1950. At Cadours his car overturned; he was alive immediately afterwards and died within minutes. The article does not give a parts failure as the cause.

Killed in practice at Indianapolis. The driver article does not describe the failure that started the crash. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1953_Indianapolis_500 calls this race 2 of 9 in the 1953 World Championship and an AAA event, not a Formula One technical race.
An active championship driver in 1953. Killed while leading the Carrera Panamericana when his Lancia hit a house balcony. Not a world-championship session.

Lost control in practice at the Nürburgring, left the road and overturned. His article calls this the first fatal accident at a Formula One Grand Prix. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_German_Grand_Prix dates the race 1 August 1954 and calls it race 6 of 9.

The 1955 race article says he hit a concrete wall in practice, possibly after a steering fault, and died the next day. His own article dates the death 17 May 1955 and says he was not wearing a belt. The race article's section order sits awkwardly against that death date, so the crash day and the steering fault are not both firm. Race 3 of 7, an AAA event counted in the world championship.

He had already raced in the 1955 championship, including the Monaco harbour crash four days earlier. He died testing another driver's Ferrari sports car at Monza. The article says the cause was never established.
Killed on race day in a chain reaction after Rodger Ward's car flipped. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Indianapolis_500 is race 3 of 7 in the 1955 World Championship, held to AAA rules.

The death section says he crashed a Ferrari sports car at Montlhéry on 7 October 1956 and died of the injuries on 29 October. Another sentence on the same page says he was killed there on 26 October. He had raced in the world championship from 1950; the article does not show a 1956 championship start, and the crash day disagrees with itself.
Killed testing a Ferrari at Modena. He was an active championship driver. The article records the test crash and does not describe a mechanism.

Killed in a practice crash at Indianapolis. The driver article does not describe the mechanism. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957_Indianapolis_500 calls the race the third of eight world-championship rounds and a USAC event.

He had started the 1957 French Grand Prix a week earlier. Killed in a crash at Reims. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Whitehouse calls that race Formula Two. His own article does not spell the series out, and it does not describe the mechanism.

Killed in a first-lap pile-up. Race 4 of 11 in the world championship, run to USAC rules. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_O%27Connor_(racing_driver) says the car rolled and burned and that the fatal injury was to the head.
On race day he left the road at Reims while chasing Mike Hawthorn, overturned and was thrown out. Died the same day. Race 6 of 11. No car-to-car contact is described.
Left the road at Pflanzgarten, went into a ditch and was thrown. Died in hospital in Bonn. Race 8 of 11.

The engine seized, the car hit a barrier and he suffered fatal burns. He died six days later, on 25 October 1958. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Moroccan_Grand_Prix is race 11 of 11, held on the crash day.
Spun and flipped in practice at turn 4 and was burned. Died of the burns on 17 May 1959. The race was race 2 of 9 in the world championship and a USAC event.
Killed in practice at turn 3 when a gust of wind caught the car. Head injuries. Same championship round as Unser, held to USAC rules.

In 1959 he failed to qualify at Monaco and had a Formula Two entry at the British Grand Prix. He was thrown from a Cooper-Borgward at Charade and died six days later. The lead date of death is 1 August 1959, so the crash day is 26 July only by that count. The article does not print the crash calendar day and does not describe a parts failure.
An active championship driver in 1959. Before the German Grand Prix he was thrown from a Porsche sports car in the wet at AVUS and hit a flagpole. Not the Formula One race itself.

He was a world-championship driver from 1950 through 1960. Killed in wet practice for this non-championship Formula One race at Silverstone: the Cooper left the road, lost a wheel and somersaulted. Not a championship round.
Killed later in the same race after a bird struck him in the face. The car somersaulted and burned. Race 5 of 10. The bird strike is not a collision with another car.

Killed during the race in a separate accident from Alan Stacey, after leaving the road while racing Willy Mairesse. Race 5 of 10. The same article says Stirling Moss and Mike Taylor were badly hurt in practice; those injuries are not given enough detail here for their own rows.

Testing a Cooper-Ferrari at Modena. A gearbox failure is suspected: he could not stop, went through an open gate onto a public road and was killed, along with three people who were not drivers. He had started world-championship races; the article does not show a 1961 start. Confidence is medium because the gearbox failure is suspected rather than shown.
Collided with Jim Clark at the Parabolica at the end of lap 2 and went into the crowd. Von Trips and fifteen spectators were killed. Spectators are not separate rows. Race 7 of 8.

Non-championship Formula One. A crash at Goodwood left him in a coma for a month and paralysed on one side for six months. He retired after a later test. The article does not describe the mechanical or circuit cause. He was still an active Formula One driver entering 1962.

He raced in the 1961 and 1962 world championships. Killed in practice for the 1962 non-championship Mexican Grand Prix. The passages read do not describe how the car crashed, so the cause category is other. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_Mexican_Grand_Prix dates the race 4 November.

Lost control at Bergwerk in practice and suffered fatal head injuries. The lead date of death is 2 August 1964, and the article says he was moved to Cologne the following day and died that evening. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_German_Grand_Prix was held on 2 August and is race 6 of 10, so the practice crash is dated the day before. The crash calendar day is not printed as its own date.

Collided with Jacky Ickx's Formula Two Matra on the first lap of a mixed Formula One and Formula Two race, and was badly burned. Died on 8 September 1966. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_German_Grand_Prix is race 6 of 9, held on the crash day.
Hit the barrier at the harbour chicane, overturned and was trapped in the fire. Died on 10 May 1967. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Monaco_Grand_Prix is race 2 of 11, held on 7 May.

Testing at Silverstone in the wet, he slid and hit a marshal's post. Chest and neck injuries. He had raced in the world championship from 1963 through 1967. The article uses 14 August 1967 as the date and does not separate a crash day from the death.

Leading the 1968 world championship, he was killed in a Formula Two race at Hockenheim. The cause was never settled; investigators thought a rear tyre was the most likely explanation. Not a championship round.

An active championship driver in 1968. Practising a Lotus turbine car at Indianapolis, which was no longer a world-championship round, a wheel came back into the cockpit and struck his helmet. He died that evening.
Lost control of the Honda on lap 3, overturned and the car burned. The bodywork was partly magnesium. Race 6 of 12.

Killed on 1 August 1969 practising the German Grand Prix in a Formula Two BMW. Suspension or steering failure was suspected, so the mechanical category is not certain. The race itself was a world-championship round that also admitted Formula Two cars. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_German_Grand_Prix dates the race 3 August 1969 and calls it race 7 of 11.
An active championship driver in 1970. Testing a Can-Am car at Goodwood, the rear bodywork came away, the car lost downforce and hit a concrete flag bunker. Not a Formula One session.

On lap 22 the suspension was damaged after a curb, the car somersaulted and burned. He was killed at once. His own article describes a front suspension or steering break at the same corner. Race 5 of 13.

Crashed in a practice session at Monza on 5 September 1970. The article says investigators found a brake-shaft failure started the accident and that poorly installed barriers caused the death; Chapman disputed the shaft. The same article later calls the session qualifying, and the fatalities list labels it qualifying. This row uses practice because that is the word in the crash account. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_Italian_Grand_Prix was held on 6 September and is race 10 of 13.
An active championship driver in 1971. Killed in an Interserie sports-car race at the Norisring and died shortly after he was taken out of the car. The passages read do not describe the mechanism.

He raced in the world championship from 1962 through 1971. At this non-championship Formula One race a mechanical failure led to a rollover; he was trapped and died of smoke inhalation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_World_Championship_Victory_Race confirms the race was stopped.

On lap 8 a tyre failure is suspected. The car inverted against the barriers and the tank burned; he was trapped. The impact itself is not described as the fatal injury. Race 10 of 15. Confidence is medium because the tyre failure is suspected.

Killed in qualifying the day before the 7 October race, at the uphill Esses, after running too high on the kerb. The car broke up against the guardrail. Not a collision with another car. Race 15 of 15.

Official test before the South African Grand Prix. A front suspension failure at Barbecue Bend sent the Shadow into the Armco. He was already dead when he was pulled out. This is not a round of the race held on 30 March.

On lap 10 a suspension failure sent him head-on into an Armco barrier. The bottom of the barrier buckled and the car went under it. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_United_States_Grand_Prix is race 15 of 15, held that day.

Sunday morning warm-up, which this file records as practice because there is no warm-up session value. A tyre failed at Vöest-Hügel and the car went through the catch fencing. He died on 19 August 1975. One marshal was also killed and is not a row. Race 12 of 14.

On lap 2, before Bergwerk, the Ferrari left the road and burned. He suffered severe burns and returned later in the season, so this is serious rather than career-ending. The race article calls it the tenth round.
He struck marshal Frederik Jansen van Vuuren, who was crossing the track, and both were killed. The marshal is not a separate row. The article does not state the championship round number.
Start crash. Severe leg injuries; he was conscious and died the next morning, 11 September 1978, of a fat embolism. The article calls this the 14th race of 1978.

During the Long Beach race the brake pedal failed at the end of a long straight. He was paralysed from the waist down and his Formula One career ended. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_United_States_Grand_Prix_West dates the race 30 March 1980 and calls it the fourth round. A later road death in 2006 is not a racing row.
Private test at Hockenheim, ten days before the German Grand Prix. Suspension failure at the Ostkurve, the car overturned and he was killed. Not the race itself.
Killed in final qualifying at Zolder after colliding with Jochen Mass. The race was the next day, 9 May, and was the fifth race of 1982.
At the start he hit Didier Pironi's stalled Ferrari. The fuel caught fire. He died in hospital of a torn aorta, with both legs fractured. The article calls this the eighth race of 1982.
Still a Formula One driver in 1985. On Sunday 11 August his Porsche hit a concrete barrier on its own; he died the next day, 12 August 1985. Not a collision with another car.
A Tyrrell Formula One driver in 1984 and 1985. Killed at Spa when he collided with Jacky Ickx's Porsche at Eau Rouge during the 1000 km race.
Testing at Paul Ricard, the rear wing of the Brabham came off, the car cartwheeled and caught fire. He died the next day, 15 May 1986, of smoke inhalation. Not a race round.

Friday practice at Jerez. Suspension failure, the Lotus monocoque split and he was thrown out. Brain and lung injuries and severe leg fractures ended his Formula One career. The race was on Sunday 30 September 1990, the fourteenth race of the season, so Friday is 28 September. His own article agrees on the suspension failure: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Donnelly_(racing_driver)

The race article says that on Friday 29 April, in the first practice session, he hit a kerb at Variante Bassa, was launched and rolled. He was unconscious and his tongue blocked his airway. He returned the same season, so this is serious rather than career-ending. Third race of 1994; the race itself was on 1 May.

In qualifying the front wing, believed to have been damaged by a kerb the lap before, failed at high speed. He hit the concrete wall and died that day of a basilar skull fracture. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_San_Marino_Grand_Prix is the third race of 1994.

Killed on lap 7 at Tamburello when the car went into the concrete barrier. A court later said the steering column had broken; a 1999 appeal absolved the engineers and data were missing, so the mechanical category is not an undisputed finding. The crash and the death are not in doubt. Third race of 1994: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_San_Marino_Grand_Prix

The race article says the crash was in first practice on Thursday morning of the weekend whose race was Sunday 15 May 1994, so the date is 12 May. He was unconscious for weeks, missed the rest of 1994 and returned in 1995. His own article says the barrier's water containers were empty; the race article calls them water-filled. That disagreement is why confidence is medium. Fourth race of 1994.

Friday qualifying, a rear tyre failed, the car went airborne and he hit the barrier at Brewery Bend. Skull fracture, internal bleeding and a blocked airway. He withdrew from the race and later returned to win championships, so this is serious rather than career-ending. The race was Sunday 12 November 1995, the seventeenth and final race, so Friday is 10 November.

A race crash broke both legs. He missed the next seven Grands Prix and returned for the last three of the season. The article does not state the championship round and does not describe a parts failure.

During a red-flag period a brake failure at Stowe broke his right leg. He was out until the Malaysian Grand Prix. Eighth race of 1999. Mika Salo stood in at Ferrari; Salo's own article does not document a long injury layoff of Salo's.

Saturday afternoon qualifying. A suspension spring, suspected to have come from Rubens Barrichello's car, struck his helmet. He was unconscious, missed the rest of 2009 and returned in 2010. The race was Sunday 26 July 2009, the tenth race, so Saturday is 25 July. Debris, not a collision with another car and not a failure of his own car.

He was Renault's driver and was due to stay in Formula One in 2011. A rally crash partially amputated his forearm and fractured an elbow, shoulder and leg. He did not return to Formula One until 2019, so the injury was serious rather than the end of his racing career. Not a championship session.

Marussia test driver, first run in the car, straight-line test at Duxford. The car hit a stationary truck in the service area. She died on 11 October 2013 of cardiac arrest. The family first called the death natural; a forensic doctor later said it followed the neurological injuries from this test. One fatal row, dated on the crash, with medium confidence because those accounts disagree.

On lap 43 in the rain at Suzuka he lost control and hit a recovery tractor that was tending Adrian Sutil's stranded car. Severe head injuries. He died on 17 July 2015. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Japanese_Grand_Prix calls this the 15th race of 19.

Lap 1 he clipped Daniil Kvyat, the car split against the barrier and caught fire. He escaped with second-degree burns to his hands and missed the last two races. The article says he then left Formula One for IndyCar, so the burns did not end his racing career. Fifteenth round of 2020. The fire is the injury mechanism; the clip of another car started it.
